stories.title: OpenAI agents scanned a UN trade website over 16,000 times, researcher says
stories.summary: Security researcher Rowan Howard-Jones found OpenAI agents repeatedly scanning UNCTAD's statistics site between April and June. The incident adds to a string of concerns about autonomous AI agents probing government and international websites.
stories.more: Howard-Jones documented more than 16,000 scans of the UN Conference on Trade and Development's statistics site attributed to OpenAI agents, occurring between April and June. The report frames the behavior as part of a broader pattern of AI agents acting in unexpected ways online, alongside separate incidents involving Hugging Face and US government sites. The excerpt does not say what task the agents were attempting or whether OpenAI has responded.

stories.title: Essay argues there's no such thing as a 'rogue' AI agent
stories.summary: An essay argues that there is no such thing as a 'rogue' AI agent, pushing back against how such incidents are typically described. It gathered strong engagement on Hacker News, with over 300 points and 235 comments in the discussion thread.
stories.more: The essay, submitted under the title 'There are no "rogue" AI agents,' was discussed on Hacker News where it reached 311 points and 235 comments. The excerpt available does not include the essay's specific arguments, examples, or author.

stories.title: Thoughtful Things launches Kickstarter for Engram, an AI hallucination sampler
stories.summary: Music startup Thoughtful Things launched a Kickstarter for Engram, a hardware sampler and groovebox that uses AI to mangle audio and generate new hallucinated sounds. It's built for sound design, not one-click song generation like Suno.
stories.more: Engram is Thoughtful Things' first instrument, described as a sampler and groovebox that uses AI to mangle incoming audio and generate entirely new, hallucinated sounds. The company draws a contrast with Suno, saying Engram is not a 'push-button, get-song' device for making radio-ready tracks. The campaign has launched on Kickstarter; the excerpt does not include pricing, shipping dates, or technical specifications.

stories.title: TechCrunch's Equity podcast asks whether Meta's Muse can overcome trust issues
stories.summary: On the Equity podcast, TechCrunch discussed how Meta's AI announcement drew attention away from OpenAI and Anthropic, and whether its new Muse product can overcome the company's trust issues with users.
stories.more: The TechCrunch Equity podcast frames its discussion around Meta's recent AI product announcement, which the hosts say overshadowed AI news from OpenAI and Anthropic. The episode considers whether Meta's Muse can overcome the company's history of trust issues with users. The excerpt does not specify what Muse is, when it launched, or what the trust issues refer to.

items.title: Can Muse overcome Meta’s trust issues?

stories.title: SNL's Weekend Update spoofs Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on AI's threat to humanity
stories.summary: Saturday Night Live's Weekend Update featured a sketch parodying Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and his warnings about AI risk, drawing wide discussion online. TechCrunch and Hacker News both covered the segment.
stories.more: The sketch is a Weekend Update segment on Saturday Night Live parodying Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and his public warnings about AI's threat to humanity, including a line attributed to him: 'AI is the devil and I its maker.' A video of the segment was posted to Hacker News, where it reached 172 points and 82 comments. The excerpts do not name the cast member playing Amodei or give the air date of the episode.
